nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe-LDH synthesis on NF
nodes.procedure: Firstly, a hydrothermal method was used to grow two-dimensional NiFe-LDH nanosheets on NF. 0.67 mmol of Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.33 mmol of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 5 mmol of CH₄N₂O, and 5 mmol of NH₄F were dissolved in 30 mL of deionized water (DIW). The solution was placed in a Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 120 °C for 12 h. As-synthesized NiFe-LDH was washed with DIW and CH₃CH₂OH, and then dried at 60 °C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: 2.2 Synthesis of NiFe-LDH precursor... Firstly, a hydrothermal method was used to grow two-dimensional NiFe-LDH nanosheets on NF.

nodes.name: Sulfur doping via ion exchange
nodes.procedure: The prepared NiFe-LDH precursor was immersed in Na₂S·9H₂O aqueous solution (0.1 M). The immersed sample was washed several times with ultrapure water to obtain the S-NiFe-LDH product.
nodes.source_text: The prepared precursor was immersed in Na₂S·9H₂O aqueous solution (0.1 M). The immersed sample was washed several times with ultrapure water to obtain the product.

nodes.name: Vapor phase selenization
nodes.procedure: S-NiFeSe₂ catalysts were prepared by vapor phase deposition. 0.5 g of Se powder and S-NiFe-LDH were added to the tube furnace. The reaction vessel was gradually heated to 300 °C at rate of 2 °C/min under Ar flow.

nodes.source_text: LSV polarization curves were measured in a representative three-electrode system in alkaline seawater (1 M KOH + seawater)... S-NiFeSe₂ exhibited excellent OER catalytic activity (367 mV, 100 mA cm⁻²)... Tafel slope of S-NiFeSe₂ is the smallest (32 mV dec⁻¹)... R_ct = 0.687 Ω... FE is close to 100 %... Zeta potential (-0.711 mV)... running at 100 mA cm⁻² for 50 h... potential increased by only 19 mV... CV and LSV curves were repeated continuously for 3,000 cycles

S-NiFeSe₂||Pt/C pair exhibits cell voltage of 1.54 V at 10 mA cm⁻² under alkaline seawater conditions... electricity-to-hydrogen conversion efficiencies exceeds 81.4 %... operate continuously for at least 100 h without significant degradation

nodes.characterization_summary: Significant diffraction peaks at 29.9°, 33.6°, 36.9°, 50.7°, 55.5°, and 57.8° correspond to the (200), (210), (211), (311), (023), and (321) planes of NiSe₂ phase. XRD pattern shows slight shift after S doping and Fe substitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S2a, significant diffraction peaks at 29.9°, 33.6°, 36.9°, 50.7°, 55.5°, and 57.8° correspond to the (200), (210), (211), (311), (023), and (321) planes of NiSe₂ (JCPDS No. 88-1711) phase, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanosheet array structure preserved after S-doping, advantageous for exposing edge active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the prepared S-NiFeSe₂ is consistent with that of NiFe-LDH and S-NiFe-LDH (Figures S3–S5). The nanosheet array structure is advantageous in exposing more edge active sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear lattice fringes with measured interlayer spacings of 0.278 nm and 0.169 nm corresponding to (210) and (320) crystal planes of NiSe₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of S-NiFeSe₂ shows clear lattice fringes, and the measured interlayer spacings are 0.278 and 0.169 nm, respectively, which are in excellent correspondence with the (210) and (320) crystal planes of NiSe₂...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Fe, Se and S are evenly distributed in S-NiFeSe₂ nanosheets. Sample contains only S, Ni, Fe, and Se elements without impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Results show that Ni, Fe, Se and S are evenly distributed in S-NiFeSe₂ nanosheets. In addition, the energy disperse spectroscopy (EDS) of S-NiFeSe₂ showed that the sample contained only S, Ni, Fe, and Se elements...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 852.8 eV and 870.1 eV (Ni⁰ from NF), 856.0 eV and 873.7 eV (Ni²⁺). Fe 2p peaks shift positively by 0.2 eV after S doping to 711.5 eV (Fe²⁺) and 714.2 eV (Fe³⁺). Se 3d peaks at 54.8 eV and 55.4 eV. S 2p peaks at 161.1 eV and 165.9 eV confirm S doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 852.8 and 870.1 eV are referred to the metallic Ni phase (Ni⁰)... The peaks of 711.5 and 714.2 eV are associated with Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺, respectively, in S-NiFeSe₂ catalyst, and the two peaks shift positively by 0.2 eV after S doping... the peaks located at 161.1 and 165.9 eV of S 2p relate to S–M (Ni and Fe) bond and sulphate (S–O)

nodes.characterization_summary: S-NiFeSe₂: -0.711 mV; NiFeSe₂: -0.362 mV; NiFe-LDH: -0.534 mV. More negative zeta potential enhances chloride ion resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with NiFeSe₂ (-0.362 mV) and NiFe-LDH (-0.534 mV), S-NiFeSe₂ has a more negatively Zeta potential (-0.711 mV), which enhances the resistance to chloride ions (Figure 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: S-NiFeSe₂ shows charge transfer resistance R_ct = 0.687 Ω, lower than RuO₂ (12.615 Ω) and NF (128 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) revealed that S-NiFeSe₂ had a charge transfer resistance (R_ct = 0.687 Ω) lower than RuO₂ (12.615 Ω) and NF (128 Ω).
